name: Blesmolfolk Warrior
body:
Just a hair above the workers and keenly aware of their insignificance, blesmolfolk warriors are frequently split between two factions: Those who seek better treatment for themselves and the workers, and those who abuse what little authority they have to mercilessly bully their inferiors. Warriors are the defenders of the hives, fierce soldiers who fight to the death to protect their leaders. In their spare time, they ready for battle, devising cunning weapons and delighting in finding new and better ways to kill. Warriors do not inherently enjoy violence, but they do enjoy being good at it.

Physical Description: Blesmolfolk warriors are much taller than workers, standing around 5’6”. They are just as round and plump, but slightly more muscular. They, too, tend to wear clothes, favoring bright colors—this is a matter of pretension as much as it is for diplomatic purposes when dealing with outsiders. Most warriors are female, but almost all are sterile. Unlike other blesmolfolk, blesmolfolk warriors have relatively short lifespans due to their more energy-intensive work, and they age at the same rate as dwarves (about 350 years). Warriors are by far the most energetic of the castes, but they still speak slowly, mostly out of habit from dealing with other blesmolfolk.

Society: Warriors serve as the bodyguards and border watchers for the blesmolfolk, and spend a good deal of time with the workers as a result—time which they tend to resent, as they know it lessens their own status. Some do seek change, and they have slightly more leeway to do so, but they lack the workers’ structured mindsets and tend not to collaborate well as a result. As such, a rebellious warrior usually finds itself fighting alone. Some warriors are, in fact, potential queens, and these are often treated very warily by the reigning monarch. Warriors make up roughly 30% of their hives, and are the second-largest caste as a result.

Relations: Like workers, warriors have relatively frequent dealings with other races, especially dwarves and evil races like morlocks and troglodytes. Because they are a caste guided to fight, however, negotiations tend to be tense. Dwarves find blesmolfolk warriors to be hostile and disrespectful, and halflings and gnomes, if they ever encounter blesmolfolk, assume that warriors are the primary caste oppressing the downtrodden workers (a simplification, of course).

Alignment and Religion: Like workers, warriors are not especially religious. They have no strong tendencies towards order or cohesion, nor towards kindness or selfishness. Most warriors are true neutral.

Adventurers: Blesmolfolk warriors are by far the most likely to exit the hive, and do well as hireswords. Others become mages or alchemists. Regardless, they almost invariably construct their own magic weaponry.

Core Traits (13 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Naturally muscular despite their fatty rolls, blesmolfolk warriors move faster than others of their kind. They are also quite canny and discerning, a trait that catches off-guard many who judge them for their slow speech. They gain +2 Strength, and +2 Intelligence. 2 RP
Size: Blesmolfolk warriors are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Speed: Blesmolfolk warriors have a base speed of 30 feet. They also have a burrow speed of 20 feet. 3 RP
Languages: Blesmolfolk warriors begin play speaking only Blesmol. Warriors with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Common, Draconic, Dwarven, Gnome, and Undercommon.
Other Traits
Pain Immunity: Blesmolfolk warriors do not feel pain and are immune to all pain-based effects. They cannot be knocked unconscious from nonlethal damage, though they can still begin to take lethal damage if their nonlethal damage is equal to their total maximum hit points. 3 RP
Craftsfolk: Blesmolfolk warriors gain a +2 racial bonus on all Craft checks to create weapons from metal or stone. They are treated as proficient with any weapon they have personally crafted. 2 RP
Quick Reactions: Blesmolfolk warriors, unlike the rest of their sluggish kind, can be terrifyingly quick and responsive when they need to be. They gain Improved Initiative as a bonus feat. 2 RP
Self-Armed: Blesmolfolk warriors gain Master Craftsman as a bonus feat, even if they do not fulfill the requirements. 3 RP
Toughness: Blesmolfolk warriors gain Toughness as a bonus feat. 2 RP
Weapon Familiarity: Blesmolfolk warriors are proficient with blesmol staves and blesmol flails. 1 RP
Insular: Blesmolfolk warriors are unused to dealing with other humanoids outside a hostile context, and tend to come across as brusque and untrusting even when they aren’t trying to be. They take a -2 penalty on Diplomacy checks when addressing non-blesmolfolk. –1 RP
Small Eyes: Blesmolfolk warriors can only see clearly out to 30 feet. Beyond that, all subjects gain concealment. Blesmolfolks take a –4 penalty on sight-based Perception checks. –5 RP
Hold Breath: Blesmolfolk warriors can hold their breath for a number of rounds equal to four times their Constitution score before risking drowning or suffocating. 1 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing warrior traits.

Frenzy: Blesmolfolk warriors live faster and harsher lives than other blesmolfolk, and some lack even the blesmolfolk’s characteristic lack of pain receptors as a consequence. They are not evolved to handle pain, however, and this can lead to maddened berserk rages where they lose nearly all sense of self-preservation. Once per day as an immediate action, a warrior can fly into a frenzy for 1 minute. This frenzy may not be ended prematurely. During this time, it gains a +2 morale bonus to Constitution and Strength and a primary bite attack that deals 1d6 damage, but a –2 penalty to AC. This trait replaces pain immunity.
Nearly Blind: Faster breeding means more chance for mutation. Some warriors are born with especially defective vision, and simply cannot see past 30 feet. All subjects beyond that range gain total concealment. They take a -4 penalty on sight-based Perception checks. Warriors with this trait gain the scent ability, as well as Blind-Fight as a bonus feat. This trait replaces small eyes.
Outcast: Due to their volatility, restlessness, and, occasionally, potential Queen status, some warriors find themselves judged ill-suited to live in the hive, and are cast out—frequently as children. This trait replaces insular and weapon familiarity.
Potential Queen: Some warriors are born with the inherent potential to be queens if subjected to the correct biological stimuli under the right circumstances. Those circumstances may never arise, but in the meantime, these warriors gain the queen’s speech trait. However they may be unwilling to use the ability for fear of being targeted by the current queen. Three times per day as a full-round action, the warrior may address any non-queen blesmolfolk within hearing with a single, sharp command. This functions as command, cast using the warrior’s Hit Dice as the caster level and its Charisma as the defining ability. This trait replaces quick reactions.
